title: First-quadrant double complexes, total complex and the two filtrations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. A *double complex*
$D^{\bullet,\bullet}$ in $\mathcal C$ is a family of objects $D^{p,q}$
($p,q\in\mathbb Z$) with morphisms

$$
 d_I:D^{p,q}\to D^{p+1,q},\qquad d_{II}:D^{p,q}\to D^{p,q+1}
$$

such that $d_I\circ d_I=0$, $d_{II}\circ d_{II}=0$ and
$d_I\circ d_{II}=d_{II}\circ d_I$. It is *first-quadrant* if $D^{p,q}=0$
unless $p\geq0$ and $q\geq0$. For each $p$ the *$p$-th column*
$(D^{p,\bullet},d_{II})$ and for each $q$ the *$q$-th row*
$(D^{\bullet,q},d_I)$ are complexes; their cohomology objects are written

$$
 H^q_{II}(D^{p,\bullet}):=H^q(D^{p,\bullet},d_{II}),\qquad
 H^p_{I}(D^{\bullet,q}):=H^p(D^{\bullet,q},d_I).
$$

Since $d_I$ commutes with $d_{II}$, it induces morphisms
$H^q_{II}(D^{p,\bullet})\to H^q_{II}(D^{p+1,\bullet})$, making
$H^q_{II}(D)$ a complex in the first index, with cohomology
$H^p_IH^q_{II}(D)$; symmetrically $d_{II}$ makes $H^p_I(D)$ a complex in the
second index, with cohomology $H^q_{II}H^p_I(D)$.

For a first-quadrant double complex the *total complex*
$\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ is

$$
 \operatorname{Tot}(D)^n:=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}D^{p,q},\qquad
 d|_{D^{p,q}}:=d_I+(-1)^pd_{II}:D^{p,q}\to D^{p+1,q}\oplus D^{p,q+1};
$$

the sum is finite (only $0\leq p\leq n$ contribute, and
$\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n=0$ for $n<0$), and $d\circ d=0$ because
$d_I^2=d_{II}^2=0$ and the two cross terms $(-1)^{p+1}d_{II}d_I$ and
$(-1)^pd_Id_{II}$ cancel.

The *first* and *second filtrations* of $\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ are the
decreasing filtrations [def-sp-filtration]

$$
 {}'F^p\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n:=\bigoplus_{i\geq p}D^{i,n-i},\qquad
 {}''F^q\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n:=\bigoplus_{j\geq q}D^{n-j,j}
$$

(filtration by the first, resp. the second, degree). Both are filtrations by
subcomplexes, since $d_I$ raises the first degree by one and preserves the
second, while $d_{II}$ preserves the first and raises the second. In total
degree $n$ both satisfy $F^0\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n=\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n$
and $F^{n+1}\operatorname{Tot}(D)^n=0$, so they are finite in each degree.
Their graded pieces are the complexes

$$
 \operatorname{gr}^p_{'F}\operatorname{Tot}(D)=D^{p,\bullet-p}
 \ \text{with differential }(-1)^pd_{II},\qquad
 \operatorname{gr}^q_{''F}\operatorname{Tot}(D)=D^{\bullet-q,q}
 \ \text{with differential }d_I .
$$

(Stacks Project, Homological Algebra: double complexes and their associated
total complexes, and the two filtrations used for the spectral sequences of
a double complex.)

proof.text: For each total degree n, index the full diagonal by pairs (i,j) with i+j=n. Its nonnegative pairs inject into the finite integer interval [0,n]. Form their finite coproduct. Extend its cofan to the whole diagonal using zero morphisms outside the nonnegative pairs. First-quadrant vanishing makes every such discarded source a zero object. Given another cofan, its maps from the nonnegative pairs determine a unique map from the finite coproduct, and its other maps agree by uniqueness from zero objects. This proves hasTotal_of_firstQuadrant, including empty diagonals.

Interval containment [q,n] ⊆ [p,n] for p≤q proves both antitone lemmas by Finset.sup_mono. The empty interval [n+1,n] proves both finite bounds. If n<0, every diagonal pair has a negative coordinate, so total.hom_ext proves that the identity on the total object is zero.

For either degree-zero filtration step, every nonzero diagonal inclusion belongs to its image supremum; an inclusion with a negative coordinate is zero and its image is bottom. Factor all coprojections through the step and combine the factors by totalDesc. The resulting map is a right inverse to the step arrow by total.hom_ext. Since the arrow is monic and split epic, it is invertible and its subobject is top.

To prove differential preservation, pull back the target step along the total differential. For each generating image, use total_d, ι_D₁, ι_D₂, d₁_eq' and d₂_eq': the horizontal and signed vertical components factor through the target step because each filtered index either stays fixed or increases by one. Addition and integer scalar multiplication preserve these factorizations. The finite supremum lies in that pullback by Finset.sup_le, giving the required subcomplex restriction.

For each graded piece, construct the projection from the total object to the distinguished diagonal summand using totalDesc, identity on that summand, and zero on the others. The original summand inclusion factors through step p; if p>n its source is zero. The projection kills step p+1, so its restriction to step p descends to the cokernel of the inclusion of step p+1. This descended map and the canonical inclusion into the cokernel are mutually inverse. One composite follows from the summand projection identity. For the other, cancel the epic cokernel projection and check on each canonical lift generating the finite image supremum: index p gives the identity, and every larger index factors through step p+1 and is killed. The private finite_sup_hom_ext proves this generating-family criterion using an equalizer and the supremum universal property. This proves both canonical graded-piece isomorphisms.

Choose the already-proved subcomplex restrictions for every filtration index. Monicity of the target step arrows shows that these restrictions commute with the inclusions of successive steps. Thus cokernel.desc defines the induced graded differential and proves its compatibility with the quotient maps. The composite of two restricted differentials is zero after postcomposition with the monic step arrow, by total d_comp_d. Cancelling the epic quotient maps proves that the induced graded differential also squares to zero.

Finally evaluate the total differential on the distinguished diagonal inclusion. In the first filtration, its horizontal term factors through step p+1 and disappears after the quotient; the surviving vertical term has coefficient p.negOnePow, which Int.coe_negOnePow identifies with (-1)^p.natAbs. In the second filtration, the signed vertical term factors through step p+1 and disappears, leaving the horizontal term. Monicity of the step arrows verifies these equalities before quotienting, and cokernel.condition finishes the two required differential formulas.

On $D^{p,q}$ one has
$d\circ d=d_I^2+(-1)^{p+1}d_{II}d_I+(-1)^pd_Id_{II}+d_{II}^2$: the first and
